classification.difficultyReason: Express both reflections as −f(−x), then use the odd-function identity to prove the equality for the whole graph.

content.prompt: Let $f(x)$ be an odd function. Prove that reflecting the graph of $f(x)$ across both the $x$- and $y$-axes will result in the exact same graph.

answer.short: Since $f(-x)=-f(x)$, the reflected rule $y=-f(-x)$ simplifies to $y=f(x)$.
answer.worked:
For an odd function, $f(-x)=-f(x)$ for every $x$ in its domain. The reflected graph has equation

$$\begin{align*} y&=-f(-x)\\ y&=-(-f(x))\\ y&=f(x). \end{align*}$$

The domain of an odd function is symmetric about zero, so the reflected equation has the same domain and gives the same graph.
